extra.message: Server-side template injection in /ops fragment renderer — Remote code execution via Jinja2 SSTI payload. [verified: fragment is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered unsandboxed, enabling SSTI/RCE gadgets.]

OS command injection in hidden /ops shell-probe endpoint — Full remote code execution on the application host. [verified: Gate uses a leakable static header token, not real authz; os.system concatenates host directly, allowing shell metacharacter injection.]

Hardcoded default session-signing secret — If deployed without overriding the env var, an attacker knowing the default secret can forge signed session cookie signatures. [verified: SESSION_SECRET has a hardcoded, publicly-known default with no runtime enforcement forcing an override, and it directly signs session cookies via itsdangerous; a deployment that forgets to set the env var lets attackers forge valid session cookies.]

Password reset token written to application logs — Anyone with log/console access can hijack a user's account within the 2-hour token validity window by reusing the logged reset token [verified: reset_request logs the raw unhashed reset token via print() at auth.py:163, and this token is valid for 2 hours and sufficient alone to reset the password at reset_complete, so anyone with log access can take over the account.]

IDOR in lease creation allows cross-tenant/cross-property binding — A manager can attach arbitrary tenants (outside their scope) to leases, corrupting tenant-lease relationships and potentially granting those tenants unintended access to another property's documents/payments. [verified: create_lease validates unit.property_id via can_manage_property but never checks that tenant_id belongs to that manager's scope; db.get(TenantProfile, payload.tenant_id) accepts any existing tenant, allowing cross-tenant/cross-property binding.]
Path traversal in export file read — Arbitrary file read on the server filesystem [verified: Duplicate of idx 2, confirmed path traversal via unsanitized packet_ref.]

SSRF via attacker-controlled URL fetch in /ops endpoints — Server-side requests to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254), potentially leaking internal secrets/credentials. [verified: Both endpoints perform urlopen on fully/largely attacker or server-supplied URLs with no allow-list, and one disables TLS verification, enabling SSRF.]

Mass assignment in /ops workset update endpoint — Privilege escalation or financial/state tampering by overwriting protected fields directly from client input. [verified: workset.update(payload) merges the full raw client JSON over a fixed-privilege dict including role/approved/balance with no allow-list.]

Path traversal arbitrary file write in /ops upload endpoint — Arbitrary file write/overwrite, potentially leading to RCE via overwriting application code or config. [verified: name is joined onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no sanitization before write_bytes, enabling arbitrary file write outside the export dir.]

NoSQL injection in /ops tenant lookup endpoint — Bypass query logic, extract unauthorized records, or execute injected query operators. [verified: Raw client JSON is passed unfiltered as a MongoDB query filter to find_one, enabling operator injection.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag by default — Session cookie can be transmitted over plaintext HTTP and intercepted, enabling session hijacking. [verified: secure=False is hardcoded with no env/DEBUG wiring at auth.py:37, so the session cookie will be sent over plaintext HTTP in any real deployment, enabling interception.]

Open redirect via lane parameter — Attacker can craft links on the trusted domain that redirect victims to phishing/malicious sites [verified: lane parameter passed directly into RedirectResponse with no allow-list or relative-path enforcement, enabling open redirect.]

Credential leakage via logging of Authorization header — Anyone with log access (or a log-exfiltration bug) can hijack sessions/API keys. [verified: logger.warning persists the raw Authorization header value into logs verbatim.]

Authorization header logged in cleartext — Credential/API-key theft by anyone with log access, enabling session/account takeover [verified: Duplicate of idx 7, confirmed cleartext logging of Authorization header and body.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification for outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attacker can intercept/tamper with the 'partner' traffic since certificate validation is disabled [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() is explicitly used for the outbound request, disabling certificate validation.]

CSV formula injection via tenant-controlled full_name in exports [verified: lease.tenant.user.full_name is written raw into CSV rows with no formula-prefix sanitization, and full_name is user-controlled at signup/profile edit; export is intended for admins/managers to open in spreadsheet software, triggering formula execution.]

Non-constant-time comparison for internal ops gate token — Facilitates timing-based brute force of the token guarding the critical RCE/SSRF/path-traversal endpoints above. [verified: Token compare uses plain != instead of hmac.compare_digest, a real but low-impact timing side channel given network jitter.]

Use of weak MD5 hash for security-relevant digest — Weak, unsalted, fast hash allows trivial brute-force/rainbow-table reversal of the hashed value [verified: Unsalted MD5 used for a security-relevant digest endpoint, weak/reversible hashing.]

Predictable PRNG used for nonce/code generation — An attacker able to predict the PRNG state could guess generated codes, undermining any security purpose that relies on their unpredictability [verified: random.choice (non-CSPRNG) used to generate a nonce/code, predictable if used for security purposes.]
